# iMirror

> iMirror is a macOS app that mirrors an Android phone or tablet to a Mac and lets you control it with mouse, trackpad and keyboard over USB or local Wi-Fi. It saves PNG screenshots and silent MP4 recordings. The screen stream goes directly between the phone and the Mac, not through any cloud service.

Made by OAW INFOTECH LLP (Our Apps World). Requires macOS 14 or later (Apple silicon and Intel) and an Android device with USB debugging or Wireless debugging (Android 11 or later) enabled. Latest version: 0.2.0. Free 14-day trial with every feature; iMirror Lifetime is a one-time $9 purchase (one person, one Mac at a time, every future update, no subscription, 14-day money-back guarantee).

## Key facts
- Connect by USB (with USB debugging authorized) or over a trusted local Wi-Fi network (Wireless debugging pairing, or USB-assisted setup).
- Click, drag and scroll on the preview to tap, swipe and scroll on the phone; Back, Home and Recents are in the toolbar; Command-V pastes Mac clipboard text into the focused Android field.
- Save PNG screenshots (⌘S) and MP4 recordings (⇧⌘R, video only, no audio) to a place you choose.
- If ADB is missing, iMirror offers Google's official Android Platform-Tools download after you accept Google's SDK terms.
- No account, no analytics, no advertising. Licence activation sends only the licence key, a hashed device identifier and the Mac's name to the vendor's licence server. Updates are signed and checked daily against github.com.
- Signed and notarized by Apple.
